answers.value: The leaseback would be a FINANCE lease (term 80% >= 75% of remaining economic life and PV of payments = 100% of fair value >= 90%), so control never passes to Harbor Trust and the transfer FAILS the sale test. Ironclad would recognize NO sale, NO $50,000 gain, and NO ROU asset: it keeps the building at its $270,000 carrying amount and keeps depreciating it over the 25-year remaining life, and records the $320,000 cash as a financial liability. Each $45,000 payment is then split between interest expense (on the financing liability) and principal reduction instead of a single straight-line lease cost; Harbor Trust records a note receivable rather than the building.

Operating leaseback, so a single straight-line lease cost of $45,000 per year is recognized; the December 31 accrual credits Lease Liability for interest and credits the ROU asset for the remainder, leaving ROU = liability at each December 31.
